title: Export authored channel-strip volume automation
scope: Emit the existing Song.VolumeAutomations records as supported GPIF channel-strip events.
acceptance: Preserve two non-default values at different positions and their linear flags.
Assert track ownership, same-position event order and exact supported wire values.
Remove only the resolved omission report; pinned AlphaTab reads equivalent values and strict export accepts the supported slice.
exclusions: Do not emit speculative GPIF DSPParam_12 channel-strip automations while the required pinned AlphaTab consumer ignores RSE/ChannelStrip/Automations.
GP3 through GP5 beat-local mix-table volume changes belong to BeatEffects.MixTableChange; they are not evidence for the distinct Song.VolumeAutomations contract.

reproduction.instructions: Reproduce via the public Go parser and GP8 exporter, then load original and output with pinned AlphaTab. The observed end-to-end difference alone does not locate the failing stage.

evidence.detail: The pinned GPIF automation dispatcher has cases only for Tempo, SyncPoint, Sound, and SustainPedal; it has no volume or DSPParam_12 case.
The pinned RSE channel-strip importer reads only the static Parameters child and ignores an Automations child.
The pinned GP5 importer converts a legacy mix-table volume byte into a beat-local AutomationType.Volume event, not a GPIF channel-strip Song.VolumeAutomations record.
Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.

resolution: Blocked against the required AlphaTab 1.8.4 oracle at revision 022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d. Its GPIF parser accepts track-level Automations but dispatches only Tempo, SyncPoint, Sound, and SustainPedal, while its RSE/ChannelStrip parser reads only static Parameters and ignores Automations. Therefore an otherwise valid DSPParam_12 channel-strip event cannot satisfy the acceptance requirement that pinned AlphaTab read equivalent volume values. The cited testdata/gp5/RSE.gp5 difference is a separate legacy domain: AlphaTab's GP3-to-GP5 importer creates a beat-local volume automation from MixTableChange, whereas Song.VolumeAutomations models GPIF channel-strip records. Keep GP8 export missing and gp8.omit.volume-automations active until acceptance names a consumer that observes the proposed wire contract or the pinned consumer gains support.
